items.title: lazy-fix
items.text:
Check and fix Python imports into PEP 810 lazy imports.

PEP 810 adds a lazy soft keyword to Python 3.15: lazy import json and lazy from pathlib import Path defer the actual import until the name is first used. lazy-fix is a CST-based (LibCST) tool that finds eligible module-level imports in your codebase and rewrites them to that syntax, so you don't have to do it by hand.

items.title: Install
items.text: uv add --dev lazy-fix

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
lazy-fix check .
lazy-fix fix .

check reports imports that should be lazy but aren't, and exits with a non-zero status if it finds any — use it as a CI gate. fix rewrites them in place; pass --diff to preview the changes without writing.

items.title: Targeting pre-3.15 projects
items.text: If a project's requires-python doesn't allow 3.15 yet, lazy-fix falls back to PEP 810's own forward-compatibility mechanism: a __lazy_modules__ list declared under the imports, rather than the lazy import syntax itself. See PEP 810 and lazy_modules.

items.title: CLI reference
items.text:
lazy-fix check <path> [options]
lazy-fix fix <path> [options]

<path> is recursed into by default; only .py files are considered. Dot-prefixed directories/files and .gitignore-matched paths are skipped.

items.title: check
items.text: Reports non-lazy imports that should be lazy, per your configuration. Writes nothing. Exits 1 if any violations are found, 0 otherwise — suitable as a CI gate.

items.title: fix
items.text:
Rewrites eligible imports to lazy form and exits 0 once done.

Flag Description --diff / --dry-run Print the changes without writing them

items.title: Exit codes
items.text: Command Exit code Meaning check 0 No violations found check 1 One or more non-lazy imports found fix 0 Fix ran (whether or not it changed anything)

items.title: Configuration reference
items.text: Config lives in a [tool.lazy-fix] section of pyproject.toml, or in a standalone lazy-fix.toml. If both are present, lazy-fix.toml wins — the same precedence rule ruff uses for ruff.toml vs [tool.ruff].

items.title: pyproject.toml
items.text:
[tool.lazy-fix]
allow = ["numpy", "pandas"]
deny = []

items.title: lazy-fix.toml
items.text:
allow = ["numpy", "pandas"]
deny = []

items.title: Options
items.text:
Key Type Description allow list of module names Modules eligible to be made lazy deny list of module names Modules that must never be made lazy

Matching is on the source module only: listing numpy governs both import numpy and from numpy import array, not individual imported names.

items.title: Python version targeting
items.text: lazy-fix reads requires-python from pyproject.toml to decide whether a file can use real lazy import syntax (3.15+) or needs the __lazy_modules__ fallback instead — see PEP 810 and lazy_modules.

items.title: Install
items.text:
uv add --dev lazy-fix

Requires Python 3.15+ to run.

items.title: Check a repository
items.text:
lazy-fix check .

Recurses from the given path, considers .py files only, and skips dot-prefixed directories/files and anything matched by .gitignore. Reports every eligible import that isn't lazy yet and exits non-zero if it finds any.

items.title: Fix a repository
items.text:
lazy-fix fix .

Rewrites eligible imports in place. Add --diff to preview the changes without writing them:

lazy-fix fix . --diff

items.title: What counts as "eligible"
items.text: An import is only rewritten if its source module is listed in your project's allow list (or not in deny, depending on how you've configured it) — see the configuration reference. lazy-fix never touches from x import *, and only rewrites module-level imports (not ones already inside a function body or conditional block).

items.title: PEP 810 and __lazy_modules__
items.text:
PEP 810, "Explicit Lazy Imports", was accepted by the Python Steering Council on 2025-11-03 and ships in Python 3.15. It adds lazy as a soft keyword in front of an import statement:

lazy import json
lazy from pathlib import Path

The import only actually runs the first time json or Path is used, not at module load time. Unlike the earlier, rejected PEP 690, this is explicit and per-statement rather than implicit and global — you opt in one statement at a time, and only at module level.

items.title: The pre-3.15 fallback: __lazy_modules__
items.text:
PEP 810 also defines a forward-compatibility marker for projects that can't require 3.15 yet:

__lazy_modules__ = ["expensive_module", "expensive_module_2"]
import expensive_module

On interpreters older than 3.15, __lazy_modules__ is inert — the import still runs eagerly. It exists so a codebase can declare which imports are intended to be lazy ahead of a 3.15 upgrade, without breaking on older interpreters in the meantime.

lazy-fix uses this as its own fallback: when a project's requires-python doesn't allow 3.15+, fix inserts or updates a __lazy_modules__ list instead of emitting lazy import syntax, and check verifies that list is present and accurate rather than checking for the syntax itself.

items.title: Pre-commit integration
items.text:
lazy-fix ships two pre-commit hooks. Add this to your project's .pre-commit-config.yaml:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/HEROgold/lazy-fix
    rev: v0.1.0 # replace with the latest tag
    hooks:
      - id: lazy-fix-check

lazy-fix-check fails the commit if it finds non-lazy imports that should be lazy, without changing anything. To have pre-commit fix them automatically instead, use lazy-fix-fix:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/HEROgold/lazy-fix
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: lazy-fix-fix

Both hooks only run against .py files that pre-commit passes them, on top of lazy-fix's own dot-prefix and .gitignore skipping.
